OWNING AN ARENA

On the Foundation zone (5.161.238.245:5000, Continuum or oss-client) any player can ask for an arena of their own. If staff say yes, the arena is yours: you choose its settings, its map and its graphics, and you can pick up to five co-mods to help run it. Everything is public: who asked for what, who decided, and why.

First: you need a password on your name

Arena requests and arena powers only work for a logged-in, password-protected name. Anyone could type your name, so the zone only trusts a name once it has been checked against a password.

How it works on Foundation: the zone keeps its own password list (there is no billing server). A name nobody has claimed yet can be used with any password, but the zone treats it as not logged in: you can play, but you cannot request or run an arena or use ?weblogin. To claim your name:

  1. Log in with your name.
  2. Type ?passwd <password> once. The name is now yours, with that password. It's first come, first served: a name someone else already claimed needs their password.
  3. Log out and back in with that password, and always use it from then on. That makes you logged in, which you need to request or own an arena or to use ?weblogin. You can change it later with ?passwd <new password>.

If you see "Your name is not authenticated" or "Only players logged in with a registered (password-protected) name …", this is the step you are missing.

Asking for an arena

Type, in any arena:

?requestarena <name> <what the arena is for>

for example ?requestarena skyrace Fast racing laps for warbirds.

  • The name is 3 to 15 characters of lowercase letters and digits. It must start with a letter and must not end in a digit. Names already in use (and public, 2v2pub, 3v3pub, 4v4pub, duel) are taken.
  • The description is up to 120 characters. Everyone can read it.
  • You can have one request waiting and own one arena at a time.

Staff (moderators and up) approve or decline it. A decline always comes with a reason. You can follow it with ?arenarequests. Once approved, go to your arena with ?go <name>.

What owners and co-mods can do

In your own arena (the powers do not work anywhere else):

  • Owner: change settings, upload the map and graphics, pick co-mods, use Continuum's settings editor (?quickfix), and the moderator tools below.
  • Co-mods (up to 5): change settings and use the moderator tools. They cannot upload files or change who the co-mods are.
  • Moderator tools (both): arena messages (?a), the game timer, locking or recycling the arena, flags and balls, setting players' ships and teams, prizes, spectating, and chat masks. Kicks, bans and zone-wide messages stay with zone staff.

Commands

For everyone

CommandWhat it does
?requestarena <name> <pitch>Ask for an arena of your own (needs a password, see above).
?arenarequestsLists waiting requests and the latest decisions.
?arenalog [name]The last 10 public events (requests, decisions, co-mod changes, …), for all arenas or one.
?myarenaShows the arena you own: status, co-mods, when someone last entered it.
?webloginSends you a one-time link to the arena web page (valid 10 minutes, works once).

Owners and co-mods, in their own arena

CommandWhat it does
?arenaset <Section:Key> <value>Change one setting, e.g. ?arenaset Warbird:BulletSpeed 3000.
?arenaget <Section:Key>Show the current value of one setting.

Owners only, in their own arena

CommandWhat it does
?comodLists your co-mods.
?comod add <player> / ?comod remove <player>Adds or removes a co-mod (public in ?arenalog).
?arenamap <file.lvl>Uploads a map from your Continuum folder; it becomes the arena's map.
?putlvz <file.lvz>Uploads a graphics file from your Continuum folder and adds it to the arena.
?quickfixContinuum's built-in settings editor for your arena.

Staff

CommandWhat it does
?approvearena <name>Approves a request: creates the arena and makes the asker its owner (moderators and up).
?declinearena <name> <reason>Declines a request; the reason is public (moderators and up).
?arenaadmin suspend <name> <reason>Closes an arena to players (super moderators and sysops).
?arenaadmin revive <name>Reopens a suspended or archived arena.
?arenaadmin transfer <name> <player>Gives the arena to another player.
?arenaadmin archive <name>Closes the arena and stores its folder away (nothing is deleted).

Uploads with ?arenamap/?putlvz need Continuum (it sends the file). With any other client, use the web page.

The web page

Type ?weblogin in game. You get a link like https://subspacefoundation.com/arena/login?t=…. Open it within 10 minutes; it works once and signs you in for 24 hours. No password is ever typed on the web.

  • Everyone can see the public page, subspacefoundation.com/arena/: every player-owned arena with its owner, co-mods and players online, waiting requests, decisions and the public log.
  • Without an arena, the signed-in page lets you send a request (same rules as ?requestarena).
  • Owners and co-mods see their arena's settings, grouped by section, with a description, default and range for each, and can change them.
  • Owners can also upload the map (.lvl) and graphics (.lvz) by drag-and-drop.

Limits

  • One arena per player, and one waiting request per player.
  • Up to 5 co-mods per arena.
  • Map: one .lvl per arena, at most 2 MB.
  • Graphics: .lvz files of at most 5 MB each, at most 10 per arena.
  • Settings: at most 20 changes per minute per arena (in game and web together). Modules settings can't be changed, and the map and graphics lists change only through uploads.
  • An arena nobody enters for 30 days is archived: it closes and its files are stored away, not deleted. Staff can bring it back with ?arenaadmin revive.
  • Every decision (request, approval, decline, transfer, suspend, revive, archive, co-mod change) is public in ?arenalog and on the web page.
